newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan calls for broad-based Afghan government.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan calls for broad-based Afghan government.

text.p: Pakistan, widely seen as wielding influence on the radical Islamic Taleban movement, called on Thursday for a broad-based government in Afghanistan.

"We are pursuing the idea of a broad-based government in principle, because we do not see how a single ethnic group or religious group, or any single group, can actually dominate Afghanistan in the long run," a Foreign Ministry spokesman said.
He told reporters this was not the time for a major peace initiative because the situation in Afghanistan, where the Taleban seized Kabul on September 27, remained "somewhat fluid".
Pakistan denies charges by the government of ousted president Burhanuddin Rabbani that it had sponsored the Taleban, which emerged from religious schools in Pakistan two years ago.
But government sources say Islamabad, which had strained ties with the Tajik-led Rabbani government, is better placed to influence the Pashtun-dominated Taleban administration.
The spokesman said Pakistan wanted all of Afghanistan's neighbours to help end the conflict there and back the formation of a broad-based government through an intra-Afghan dialogue.
"This seems to us to be the only logical and sensible course which all members of the international community should take."
The spokesman said Pakistan was in contact with powerful Uzbek chief General Abdul Rashid Dostum, who controls six northern provinces, but gave no details.

He said Pakistan had also been in touch with Russia, Iran, Turkey and Central Asian states and saw no harm in a promise of humanitarian aid to northern Afghanistan by Russia and four other members of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS).

"We have always respected the legitimate concerns and interests of all the neighbours of Afghanistan. We are also not averse to humanitarian help being given to Afghanistan by these countries," he said.
But the spokesman said concern expressed by some CIS countries that the Taleban militants now ruling Kabul might eventually threaten their borders was misplaced.
"We ourselves see no reason for Afghanistan to confront or endanger any of the CIS states. The Taleban have not demonstrated any ill-will or aggression towards CIS states."

He said the Taleban had reached the border of Turkmenistan in September 1995 after capturing the western province of Herat, but had been "conducting normal relations with Turkmenistan and making peace with the forces of General Dostum".
He said Pakistan wanted all the wealthy countries that showed interest in Afghanistan during the Soviet occupation in the 1980s to help reconstruct the war-shattered country.
